symbols.sig: const BADGE_FONT = '-apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, "SF Pro Text", "SF Pro", "Segoe UI", Roboto, sans-serif'

symbols.name: measureInk
symbols.sig: export function measureInk( text: string, font: { style: string; weight: string; sizePx: number; family: string },): { left: number; right: number; ascent: number; descent: number; weightX: number } | null

params.name: font
params.type: { style: string; weight: string; sizePx: number; family: string }

symbols.returns: { left: number; right: number; ascent: number; descent: number; weightX: number } | null
doc: I find the visible ink of a text, in CSS px, by DRAWING it on a hidden canvas at 16x resolution and reading which pixels are painted. (The canvas's own "actualBoundingBox" numbers are not reliable for this: in some browsers they are the font's reserved box rounded to whole pixels, not the ink.) I draw the text at its REAL font size and only MAGNIFY it by a transform: a system font such as SF Pro changes its design with the size (a "Text" cut for small sizes, a "Display" cut for large ones), so drawing it 16 times bigger would measure a different design from the one on screen. The result uses the same terms as actualBoundingBox*: left/right are distances from the text's origin (left is positive when the ink reaches LEFT of the origin), ascent/descent are distances above/below the baseline; weightX is the distance from the origin to the ink's centre of weight (the average position of the painted pixels, each counted by how much of it is painted). null when nothing is drawn.
